column_header_verbatim: Robust standard errors model with imputation and inverse probability weighting
rule_from_plan: §9.1 (ruling R9): microbiologically confirmed pulmonary TB per 100,000 aged >= 15 years, with 95% CI
note: Table 20 ('Prevalence of microbiologically confirmed pulmonary TB among population aged ≥ 15 years in India (per 100 000 population) by gender, age group and states') prints two measures for each of the 20 state groups, both microbiologically confirmed pulmonary TB per 100,000 aged >= 15 years: 'Crude Prevalence' (exact binomial CI) and the column used here. The report calls the latter its best estimate ('The best estimates of the microbiologically confirmed PTB in India was 316 (290-342) per lakh population for the year 2021.', PDF p. 90; 'The best estimates of the microbiologically confirmed PTB for the 20 state groups are given in the figure 20.', PDF p. 93) and plots it in Figure 20 (PDF p. 94). Checked equal to Table 21's first column (PDF p. 95) and annexure 9.2 Model 6 (PDF pp. 143-144). This column is the survey's primary-outcome estimator: primary objective, PDF p. 20 ('point prevalence of microbiologically confirmed pulmonary TB among persons aged ≥15 years individually for 20 states / state groups'); estimation method for the primary outcome, PDF pp. 47–48 (svy with inverse probability weighting and post-stratification, logistic regression with robust standard errors, multiple imputation with Rubin's rules). The crude column is an unweighted exact-binomial figure and is not used.
